papers.title: URCHIN: A Horizontal Spiking Language Model for Data-Constrained Pretraining
papers.desc: Recirculates each token through one shared spiking connectome to a fixed point, supporting equivalent parallel-scan training and event-driven recurrent inference.

papers.title: Finite-Time Node Separation in Recurrent Graph Neural Networks with Persistent Gaussian Perturbations
papers.desc: Proves finite-time separation, near-collision bounds, and distributional equivariance for recurrent GNNs that reuse one message-passing operator with persistent Gaussian perturbations.

papers.title: T-LoopFormer: Token-Level Elastic-Depth Looped Transformers for Latent Reasoning With Dynamic Routing
papers.desc: Reuses a shared Transformer stack while routing each token to its own recursion depth, with recursion-wise KV caches that avoid recomputing tokens after they exit.

papers.title: Same path, different: a mechanistic comparison of looped and stacked transformer encoders on 12-lead ECG
papers.desc: Compares a Transformer block reused twelve times with a twelve-layer untied encoder on ECG classification, finding parameter-efficient accuracy parity but distinct representation dynamics.

papers.title: Recurrent Graph Neural Networks with Set-Based Aggregation
papers.desc: Characterizes set-aggregation recurrent GNNs that iterate one shared block to convergence through an effective two-way equivalence with a fixed-point logic fragment supporting reachability and safety.

papers.title: Certified Inference and Training for Deep Equilibrium Networks: A Continuation Framework with Polynomial Complexity Guarantees
papers.desc: Develops a certified continuation framework for deep equilibrium inference and training, using homotopy and rounded Newton tracking to obtain polynomial bit-complexity guarantees on a formally specified promise class.

papers.title: Right Direction, Wrong Step: Geometric Analysis of Finite-Step Failure in Looped Transformers
papers.desc: Separates update direction from displacement scale in looped Transformers, showing that some harmful full recurrent steps begin along locally useful directions and can recover reference utility when shortened.

papers.title: LoopSpec: Pipelined Self-Speculative Decoding for Looped Transformers
papers.desc: Introduces a training-free self-speculative decoding pipeline for looped Transformers that drafts from intermediate recurrent states, overlaps drafting with final-depth verification, and preserves the target distribution while substantially reducing latency.

papers.title: Persistent Recurrent Memory Between Transformer Layers - Improves Language Model Generalization
papers.desc: Inserts a persistent latent state between Transformer halves and recursively reuses one GRU update within each forward pass, with controlled small-scale experiments attributing improved generalization to the recurrent memory topology.

papers.title: How Model Growth, Recursion, and Boundary Operators Influence Scaling Exponents
papers.desc: Studies compute-optimal scaling in prelude-core-coda Transformers, finding that tied loop growth improves the fitted scaling exponent while trailing untied growth by a constant factor, and that more loops regularize data-constrained multi-epoch training.

papers.title: LSTM-UT and Recurrent-Depth Transformers on Cellular Automata
papers.desc: Compares recurrent-depth Transformer memory designs on cellular automata and delayed recall, then introduces bounded gated LSTM-UT to improve unseen-depth extrapolation and retrieval over current-state and expanding-cache baselines.

papers.title: CoRELoop: Parameter-Efficient Controlled Recurrent Refinement for Audio Deepfake Detection
papers.desc: Reuses a frozen audio encoder core through bridged, gated recurrent passes with loop-specific low-rank adaptation and adaptive halting, improving cross-domain deepfake detection while training only lightweight modules.

papers.title: Beyond Depth Truncation: Controlled Evaluation of Depth Utilization in Recursive Language Models
papers.desc: Introduces the Depth Control Protocol for weight-shared recurrent language models, separating block-application, distinct-depth, and readout-calibration effects that ordinary inference-time truncation conflates.

papers.title: PhGS: Post-Hoc Pruning and Refinement of Single-View Feed-Forward 3D Gaussian Reconstructions
papers.desc: Adds a trainable shared recurrent refiner, applied for four steps after a frozen single-view 3D Gaussian backbone, and prunes roughly half of the predicted Gaussians while largely preserving the reported reconstruction quality.

papers.title: REFINEPPO: Learning Continuous Control Policies by Iterative Action Refinement
papers.desc: Extends PPO with a shared residual policy network that repeatedly refines an action proposal within one policy forward process, improving performance on 13 of 14 continuous-control tasks in the reported evaluation.

papers.title: Prediction Dynamics in Depth-Recurrent Language Models
papers.desc: Decomposes prediction margins across repeated applications of a shared language-model block and identifies stable prediction directions and token pairings, reducing the mean earliest qualifying recurrent depth by 22.5 to 34.4 percent in the reported analyses.

papers.title: Neural Cellular Automata Learn General Features in their Hidden Channels
papers.desc: Analyzes the hidden channels of a roughly 9,800-parameter neural cellular automaton whose learned update rule is reused over recurrent steps, finding orthogonal, scale-invariant topological features that transfer across few-shot and scale-varied MNIST tasks.

papers.title: Dissecting Hierarchical Reasoning Models: A Mechanistic Study
papers.desc: Uses causal state interventions, probes, and sparse autoencoders to analyze hierarchical recurrent reasoning, finding constraint-aware iterative refinement while showing that a simpler single-state recurrent Transformer can attain comparable behavior.

papers.title: WaveFront Decoding: Parallelized Self-Speculative Decoding for Looped Language Models
papers.desc: Parallelizes self-speculative decoding for looped language models by batching tokens at different sequence positions and recurrence depths, reporting 2.42 times speedup on Ouro and 3.54 times on Huginn, rising to 4.81 times with KV sharing.

papers.title: Q-DEQ: Discrete Solving and Quantization for Deep Equilibrium Models in Time Series Forecasting under Edge Deployment Coding Constraints
papers.desc: Combines a QUBO-formulated local solver with W8A8 quantization for deep-equilibrium time-series forecasting, preserving accuracy within a narrow MSE range while reducing parameter count by 1.80 to 3.82 times and storage by 4.3 to 12.8 times for edge deployment.

papers.title: LoopCD: Loop-wise Contrastive Decoding for Improving Reasoning in Looped Language Models
papers.desc: Introduces loop-wise contrastive decoding, which contrasts predictions from successive applications of a shared recurrent language-model block to suppress premature answers, improving reasoning accuracy by 1.06 to 6.71 percentage points while retaining roughly 0.98 to 0.99 times baseline throughput.

papers.title: Statistical Gains from Looped Estimation under Parameter Budgets
papers.desc: Establishes Hellinger-risk upper and minimax lower bounds for estimators that repeatedly reuse a parameter-budgeted map, showing regimes where looped estimation improves statistically over non-looped alternatives and approaches minimax rates with bounded parameters.

papers.title: When Recursive Models Finish Computing
papers.desc: Studies when Tiny Recursive Models have effectively completed their computation, showing that extending the same attention-and-MLP recurrence from 16 to 512 steps raises cumulative exact Sudoku solve rates and linking convergence to anisotropic stability along the model trajectory.

papers.title: LexLattice: Multilingual Extractive Summarization via Neural Cellular Automata on Document Hierarchies
papers.desc: Places frozen paragraph embeddings of a legal act on a 2D lattice and consolidates them with a masked neural cellular automaton that applies one shared local update for eight steps, reaching state-of-the-art ROUGE across all 24 EUR-Lex-Sum languages with a 1.8M-parameter consolidator.

papers.title: Attention Routing Stabilizes Early: Working-Set Inference for Recurrent Language Models
papers.desc: Finds that attention support in recurrent-depth language models stabilizes earlier than hidden states and introduces WISE, a training-free method that uses global attention in early recurrent steps and reuses the discovered sparse working set later, reaching up to 1.76 times attention speedup at 4K context.

papers.title: Stream Recursion Model (SRM)
papers.desc: Modifies the Hierarchical Reasoning Model into a multi-stream recursive architecture whose layers repeatedly call shared per-stream step functions, aiming at scalable mechanistic interpretability while matching GPT-2 on a per-parameter basis and revealing specialized stream dynamics.

papers.title: On Growth and Form, and Function: Reusable Regulatory Handles Control Phenotypic Variation
papers.desc: Applies low-rank adaptation to pretrained neural cellular automata whose shared local update rule grows morphologies from a single cell, showing rank-one adapters implement scaling transformations that combine, transfer zero-shot across phenotypes, and reveal low-dimensional control directions.

papers.title: Depth through recurrence: Looped transformers for flow-matching TTS
papers.desc: Compares seven weight-reuse layouts for flow-matching text-to-speech Transformers at a fixed 18 block calls, finding that applying nine blocks twice keeps competitive intelligibility and speaker similarity with 47.1 percent fewer parameters, and that reuse order and placement shape quality across sampling budgets.

papers.title: FlashLoop: Fast and Memory-Efficient Looped Transformers via Lazy Updates
papers.desc: Training-free inference framework for looped Transformers that exploits cross-loop redundancy with token-sparse updates, loop-aware sparse attention, and KV-residual quantization, reporting lossless accuracy with up to 1.64 times end-to-end speedup and 6 times KV-cache reduction on Ouro and Huginn.

papers.title: Fixed Points Without Fixed Diffusion: Implicit Neural Sheaves for Convergent Test-Time Computation
papers.desc: Introduces SheafDEQ, a subhomogeneous deep-equilibrium graph network whose node states are fixed points of learned, edge-dependent neural-sheaf message passing, with a proof of a unique globally attracting equilibrium reachable by fixed-point iteration and gains over fixed-propagation implicit GNN baselines on long-range and heterophilic tasks.

papers.title: Quantizing Looped Transformers: Feedback Exposure and Calibration Blindness
papers.desc: Diagnoses two failure modes of post-training quantization for looped Transformers, feedback exposure at non-residual loop-entry layers and calibration blindness from step-0-only GPTQ Hessians, and shows that accumulating the Hessian across recurrence steps beats one-step GPTQ and round-to-nearest on nine checkpoints from seven looped architectures, recovering bf16-level accuracy on Huginn.

papers.title: Programs-of-Layers in LLMs through the Lens of Cortical Areas
papers.desc: Reproduces program-of-layers (PoLar) search across five LLMs, confirming that inputs benefit from skipping and repeating contiguous layer blocks within one forward pass, that harder questions need more layer repeats, and that a few generic programs cover most questions, while failing to replicate the learned router's single-shot gains.

papers.title: Beyond the Training Horizon: Mechanisms and Limits of Length Generalization in Looped Transformers
papers.desc: Mechanistically compares two looped-Transformer recurrence-training schemes on polynomial iteration, finite-state composition, and knowledge-graph traversal, showing that one updates a state at a fixed readout while the other propagates an advancing computational frontier, and that both degrade at depths beyond training because readout, progress cues, or state propagation become unreliable.

papers.title: Structured Sparse Memory for Recurrent Reasoning
papers.desc: Presents CHARM, a compact ARC model that pairs a recurrent reasoning backbone with a compositional sparse task embedding (CoSE) that cuts learned task-memory parameters by over 90 percent, finds that recurrent depth helps only when balanced with learning horizon, and reports 84 percent pass@2 on ARC-AGI-1 and 46.7 percent on ARC-AGI-2 public evaluation.

papers.title: LoopTrack: A Simple Baseline for Parameter-Efficient Transformer Tracking
papers.desc: Proposes LoopTrack, a visual object tracker that repeatedly applies a shared set of Transformer blocks for template-search interaction instead of stacking separately parameterized blocks, adding target-aware looping and a gated cross-frame target memory to reduce parameters while keeping multiple rounds of feature interaction.

papers.title: Reasoning on the Simplex: Geometric Fixed-Point Models
papers.desc: Introduces Geometric Fixed-Point Reasoning, which iterates a weight-tied map on a product of simplices so the recurrent state is itself the categorical prediction and a fixed point exists for any parameters; a 7M-parameter model reaches 95.1 percent on Sudoku-Extreme and 92.0 percent on Maze-Hard, and a 201M language model with 24 Picard steps beats GPT-2 small on four zero-shot tasks.

papers.title: Loop Dropout: Regularizing Shared Updates in Looped Language Models
papers.desc: Finds that LoRA adapters shared across the loops of a looped language model are biased toward late loop positions and proposes Loop Dropout, which randomly masks per-loop adapter applications with inverse-survival rescaling, improving mathematical reasoning, instruction tuning, and code generation with no extra inference cost.

papers.title: FlexLoop: Depth-Elastic Looped Policies for Adaptive Test-Time Computation in Deep RL
papers.desc: Shows that pretrained looped RL policies specialize to their trained recurrent depth and proposes FlexLoop, a post-training method using adjacent-depth policy distillation so decisions stay reliable at shallower depths and can stop per state via recurrent-depth consistency, evaluated on 30 long-horizon goal-conditioned environments.

papers.title: Shallow Queries, Mature Values: Depth-Asynchronous Self-Speculation for Looped Transformers
papers.desc: Observes that queries and keys in looped Transformers converge to their final-depth values earlier than values do, and introduces Depth-Asynchronous Self-Speculation, where shallow drafts read full-depth prefix values; the DAS-Wave variant gives 4.00 to 6.96 times mean throughput speedup over full-depth decoding on math and code workloads.

papers.title: Compute Time Scaling with Recursive Models for Combinatorial Optimization
papers.desc: Adapts tiny recursive models to combinatorial optimization with a graph-aware network that iterates a latent state under adaptive halting and scales both recursion depth and parallel sampling, beating diffusion-based solvers on TSP from 500 to 10,000 cities at lower cost and exploring self-relabeling as a training signal.

papers.title: Multi-Attractor GNNs: Set-Valued Expressivity Beyond Unique Equilibria
papers.desc: Proves that allowing multiple equilibria lets one weight-tied recurrent message-passing GNN represent set-valued permutation-equivariant maps, with different initializations converging to different valid solutions, and learns such dynamics without solution labels on Ising ground states, protein module detection, and chemical reaction steady states.

papers.title: Improving Test-Time Scaling with Adaptive Looped Transformers
papers.desc: Measures test-time scaling of looped Transformers as accuracy gain per doubling of decoding FLOPs and proposes TaH2, which post-trains a looped backbone with an iteration decider supervised by lookahead depth labels so only tokens that benefit get extra iterations, improving the AIME accuracy-compute slope by 53 percent over the non-looped baseline.

papers.title: How to Loop MoE: Flatten the Experts, Untie the Attention
papers.desc: Proposes Foil for looped mixture-of-experts models, which halves the expert layers while doubling experts per layer and passes, and gives each pass its own attention while experts and routers stay shared; at equal parameters and compute, Foil lowers pretraining loss over an unflattened looped MoE baseline through 100B tokens.

papers.title: LoopICL: Looping a single transformer block to solve tabular tasks
papers.desc: Introduces LoopICL, a tabular in-context-learning foundation model built from a single transformer block unrolled with cell and row streams and a learned exit gate; it matches TabICLv2 on TabArena and TALENT at equal FLOPs with nearly 90% fewer parameters and lets users trade inference cost for accuracy.

papers.title: What Makes Recurrence Effective in Looped Language Models?
papers.desc: Controlled study of when recurrence helps looped language models: extra loops can improve reasoning beyond the training horizon while degrading knowledge, layer and iteration allocation matters beyond effective depth, and channel-wise history-state injection with timestep conditioning is more robust than initial-state injection across inference budgets.

papers.title: Scheduling Recursive Reasoning in Looped Transformers
papers.desc: Proposes TAPS, a scheduler that adapts the step size of each shared-parameter recurrent update online by balancing persistent progress against fluctuation, improving terminal accuracy of looped reasoning models without retraining and giving up to 1.56x wall-clock speedup at matched accuracy when used in training.

papers.title: Looped Transformers as Optimizers
papers.desc: Views the looped hidden state as a fast weight and derives loop transitions of looped Transformers as local optimizer updates toward implicit targets; aligning existing transitions and the resulting OperLoop (weight decay, adaptive step size, delta objective) improve commonsense and generative performance over looped and non-looped baselines at matched training FLOPs.

papers.title: Looped Actor: Depth-Recurrent Reasoning Models for Reinforcement Learning
papers.desc: Introduces Looped Actor, a transformer policy that repeatedly applies a shared block to refine a latent toward a fixed point with state-dependent loop counts; across 22 tasks in six online and offline RL environments it matches or exceeds an untied baseline with 16x more parameters, with largest gains where planning is needed.

papers.title: Thinking in Depth, Speaking Directly: Recurrent Latent Reasoning for Paralinguistically Grounded Spoken Dialogue
papers.desc: Introduces LoopSLM, a spoken language model that reuses a decoder block for latent reasoning with acoustic grounding at every pass and a two-stage training recipe; on EchoMind it improves paralinguistic reasoning by over 20 points versus CoT fine-tuning while generating 64.5% fewer tokens at half the latency.

papers.title: Beyond Interaction Capacity: Estimator Scaling with Recursive Models for CTR Prediction
papers.desc: Proposes RECAP, a CTR model whose cross-network towers share core interaction weights across recursive steps and aggregate predictions over inference-time adapter routes, combining this with distillation and EMA as parameter-efficient estimator scaling to reach state-of-the-art accuracy on standard CTR benchmarks.

papers.title: Edge-RecViT: Efficient Vision Transformer via Semantic-Refined Dynamic Recursion
papers.desc: Introduces Edge-RecViT, combining a fully shared recursive ViT hidden layer with an edge-aware token ranker that allocates per-token depth and early exits for parameter- and FLOP-efficient vision.

papers.title: Implicitly-Defined Neural Networks for Sequence Labeling
papers.desc: Defines sequence hidden states jointly through a learned implicit system and solves the coupled nonlinear equations to enable non-causal bidirectional interactions for sequence labeling.

papers.title: ChainGPT: Dual-Reasoning Model with Recurrent Depth and Multi-Rank State Updates
papers.desc: Introduces ChainGPT, a dual-reasoning recurrent-depth architecture that combines multi-substep state updates and state-guided sparse attention to move reasoning into latent computation, with adaptive stopping as a supporting mechanism.

papers.title: MoDr: Mixture-of-Depth-Recurrent Transformers for Test-Time Reasoning
papers.desc: Introduces MoDr, which adds multi-branch routing to a depth-recurrent Transformer so looped models can explore solution paths more adaptively at test time.

papers.title: Polymorphic Universal Transformer
papers.desc: Introduces the Polymorphic Universal Transformer, adding conditional sparse subspaces and uncertainty-aware depth scheduling to shared-parameter recurrence to reduce compute while mitigating representational collapse.

papers.title: Universal Speech Transformer
papers.desc: Adapts the Universal Transformer to speech recognition with shared iterative encoder and decoder computation, dynamic depth, one-time positional encoding, and full hidden-state updates.
